text:
Elaine: Quick ask — proposing we reduce retention for 'debug' service logs from 30d -> 7d to save costs, and instead keep a scrubbed subset to the SIEM for 90d for detection. Thoughts?

Raj: Why 7d specifically? Forensics often needs >7d for multi-stage incidents. Are you thinking full raw logs get deleted after 7d or archived?

Elaine: Raw debug logs would be deleted after 7d. Forensics would rely on a cold-archive (S3 Glacier-like) snapshot we only restore with an approved incident ticket. SIEM gets tokenized/anonymized fields for continuity of detection.

Tara: Implementation Qs: how do we mark events as 'scrubbable' vs 'non-scrubbable'? We need a pipeline tag so the scrubber can drop PII (ip, user_email) and keep metadata. Also need a clear list of fields to scrub.

Raj: Agree on pipeline tagging. My concern: some debug logs include request IDs and stack traces that are critical for root-cause. If we scrub too aggressively we lose signal. Suggest we keep complete traces for a small subset: sampled 1% and all traces flagged as "incident-related" by the agent.

Samir: From ops side — export flow to SIEM needs KMS unwrap consideration. Current exporter uses a CMK that the exporter role can Decrypt for streaming to Splunk. If we keep a separate cold-archive CMK (different key policy), we can gate access via a ticketed workflow.

Elaine: Good — so plan: 1) Debug raw -> 7d live then cold-archive under archive-CMK; 2) SIEM gets scrubbed stream (90d) encrypted with siem-CMK; 3) 1% full-sample kept live for 30d for debugging; 4) JIT unarchive with audit ticket.

Tara: RBAC change needed: currently SRE-readers can query raw-logs. Proposed new groups: 'raw-log-readers' (oncall + incident responders), 'scrubbed-readers' (sec, SOC, devs). Need migration and a brief window where both exist. Who owns the RBAC PR?

Raj: I can own the RBAC PR and the IAM policies. One question: what about third-party root-cause collaboration? Partner vendors sometimes need trace access for 30d. We should include an export entitlements workflow (time-limited presigned archive URLs + CMK rewrap) rather than adding them to raw-log-readers.

Elaine: +1 for presigned + CMK rewrap approach. That keeps long-term entitlements minimal.

sec-bot: Policy doc link: <https://redwood.app/policy/log-retention-scrub-guidelines> (read-only) :link:

Samir: For the JIT unarchive flow — I'll add a ticket template to the incident runbook: reason, duration, approver, auditor, CMK id. We should add an automatic notification to security and log the unwrap operation in the audit trail.

Tara: Small ask — can we include a test export job so SOC can validate scrub rules? We don't want to roll this out blind.

Elaine: Yes. Action items: (1) Raj -> RBAC PR + IAM policies (due Mon), (2) Samir -> ticket template & exporter CMK plan (due Wed), (3) Tara -> scrub rule doc + test export harness (due Tue), (4) Elaine -> update policy doc and run stakeholder review (due Thu). I'll send invites for a short sync.

Raj: Noted. Also will add a minimal sampling switch in the pipeline config: sample_rate=0.01 default, override by agent flag.

Samir: Will ensure exporter rotates keys monthly and add audit logs for Decrypt API calls.

Elaine: Great. If nobody objects I'll start the sync invite and PR branches. :thumbsup:

Tara: No objections from me.

Raj: Fine by me.

sec-bot: Reminder: all KMS unwrap events are forwarded to sec-audit for 365d retention.
